Dublin, OH – FST Logistics, a leading third-party logistics provider specializing in temperature-controlled transportation, retail consolidation, warehousing and supply chain solutions, is proud to announce the expansion of its Central Ohio footprint with the opening of a new facility in West Jefferson, Ohio. As we continue to grow our ESOP and create new jobs, we’re proud to strengthen our presence in Central Ohio and continue delivering excellence for our customers for years to come,” said Brad Wright, President of FST Logistics. 

The additional capacity will support FST’s broad range of warehousing and supply chain services, including storage, distribution, retail consolidation and other customized logistics solutions. The facility provides FST with the ability to accommodate customers with varying inventory and distribution requirements while offering a strategic Central Ohio location to support their supply chain operations. 

The facility provides convenient access to major transportation routes and strengthens FST’s ability to serve customers throughout Central Ohio and key national markets. The expansion further enhances FST’s scalable warehousing capabilities while maintaining the company’s commitment to customer service, operational flexibility and supply chain efficiency.

# Maersk: Logistics center in the heart of Germany

 Sep 23, 2026 at 4:44 PM 

 

Maersk has opened a new logistics center in Herleshausen, Hesse, specifically developed for a customer from the online retail sector. The site, located in the „Panattoni Park Bad Hersfeld East,“ offers a total area of 71,800 m², of which 62,800 m² is for storage purposes, 2,900 m² for offices, and 6,100 m² mezzanine. The storage racks, which reach a height of almost 12 m, have been filled with various products since August. The outbound operation for distributing goods to German and European delivery centers has now begun.

### Central location and job creation

The site in Herleshausen is directly located on the A4 motorway, an important transport axis in Germany. Ole Trumpfheller, head of Maersk Area Northern Europe Continent, emphasizes the significance of the location as a central hub for goods flows within Germany and into neighboring European markets. „Our latest logistics center is an ideal addition to our portfolio in Germany given the strong growth of our contract logistics business and supports our integrator focus,“ says Trumpfheller.

After the full ramp-up of the logistics center, between 300 and 400 jobs will be created in the region. During the peak season of online retail, which lasts from October to December, the number of employees can temporarily rise to up to 1,000. Currently, 150 employees are already working at the new site, and numerous additional job openings are planned in the coming weeks.

The logistics center is equipped with a photovoltaic system and utilizes a rainwater harvesting system. Additionally, charging stations for electric vehicles are available, and special break areas for employees have been created. #### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

The facility has about 100 workers, a figure he expects to reach 150 by March 2027. Seasonal hiring could push employment toward 200 during the Black Friday peak before tapering in January.

#### G10’s real estate

The move consolidates two smaller warehouses — a 150,000-square-foot building in Twin Lakes and a 50,000-square-foot site in New Berlin — into one operation.

G10 is giving up both former buildings rather than keeping them as backup capacity, according to the chief executive. The company owns the Twin Lakes site, which is being leased to Allied Plastics. The New Berlin property is owned by one of Becker’s business partners and is being turned over to another venture.

Kenosha will be one of three anchor hubs in G10’s national network, he said, alongside a Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, warehouse scheduled to open in October and a planned Ontario, Canada, facility targeted for 2027.

The company is also exploring a location in Southern California.

G10 has grown from a 10,000-square-foot hangar in Lake Geneva in 2009 into a fulfillment operation that stores, processes and ships products for manufacturers and brands across multiple sales channels.

Maersk has leased the facility on a long-term basis to expand its contract logistics operations. According to Ole Trumpfheller, Managing Director of Maersk Area Northern Europe Continent, Herleshausen offers a central location for the movement of goods across Germany and into neighboring European markets. Once fully operational, the site is expected to employ 300–400 permanent workers. During the peak online retail season from October to December, the workforce could increase to around 1,000 employees. Around 150 people are currently working at the site, with recruitment continuing.

The new Maersk logistics center is equipped with solar panels, a rainwater collection system and charging infrastructure for electric vehicles. Dedicated well-being areas have also been provided for employees. The facility is targeting Gold certification from the German Sustainable Building Council (DGNB). The opening of the Herleshausen site expands Maersk’s logistics footprint in Germany and supports the company’s strategy of providing integrated logistics solutions to its customers.
